### Observed differences

- In the later window, activities A33, A34, A36, A37, A38, A39, A40 and A41 each appear in about half of the traces (roughly 50 in 100) instead of in all traces (100 in 100) before. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008]
- A30 still appears in every trace, but its position shifts later in the trace (mean from about 0.58 to 0.66 of the trace length). [POS001]
- The activities split into two groups: A33, A34, A36, A37 and A38, A39, A40, A41. Before, any activity from one group co‑occurred with any activity from the other group in all traces; after, such pairs almost never co‑occur (about 1–2 in 100 traces), with each activity appearing alone in about half the traces. [REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL026, REL027, REL028, REL029, REL031, REL032, REL033, REL034, REL035, REL036, REL037, REL038]
- Within each group, the activities still co‑occur together in about half the traces, and both are absent in about half (e.g., A33 with A34: co‑occurrence about 50%, neither about 48%). [REL017, REL018, REL019, REL039, REL040, REL041, REL042, REL043, REL044]
- A31, which used to follow the whole block, now follows either branch: it appears in all traces, but co‑occurs with each branch in about half the traces. [REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016]
- The distance between A30 and the second group (A38–A41) decreased from 5 steps to 1–4 steps; similarly, the distance between the first group (A33–A37) and A31 decreased from 5 steps to 1–4 steps. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG008, LAG013, LAG017]
- Positions of the first group (A33, A34, A36, A37) shifted later (mean +0.07 to +0.09), while positions of the second group (A39, A40, A41) shifted earlier (mean −0.03 to −0.05). [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that a single sequential block of activities (A33–A41) was replaced by a choice between two alternative sub‑blocks: one containing A33, A34, A36, A37 and the other containing A38, A39, A40, A41, both still preceded by A30 and followed by A31. The supporting signs are consistent: each activity’s participation halved, the two groups became mutually exclusive, A31 still appears in all traces, and the lag distances and position shifts match the shorter branch structure. A competing explanation—that activities are simply skipped independently—is unlikely because the mutual exclusivity between the two groups is clean and systematic, and A31’s presence in all traces argues against a general shortening of cases. Some lag items rest on very few observations in the later window, but the core pattern is corroborated by many independent indicators. [OCC001–OCC008, REL020–REL023, REL026–REL029, REL031–REL038, REL009–REL016, LAG001–LAG005, LAG008, LAG013, LAG017, POS001–POS008]
